payload.name: Knowledge-Sharing Activity Retrieval
payload.description: When a question asks what someone does to share knowledge, teach, mentor, or help others develop, use concrete activity verbs when searching and supplement after finding one activity.
content: When a question asks how someone shares knowledge, teaches, mentors, or helps others develop, do not search only the abstract phrase 'share knowledge'. Run hybrid searches using concrete activity terms such as 'gives seminars', 'teaches', 'mentors', 'coaches', 'trains', 'workshops', 'presents', and 'helps others'.
Include memory kinds event and plan; knowledge-sharing actions are often stored as specific events or planned sessions rather than as general knowledge statements.
After finding one activity, run at least one additional search with a different concrete activity verb before answering, because a person may share knowledge in multiple distinct ways.
Stop after two or three distinct query attempts yield no new activity, and answer only from visible evidence.

solves: Access retrieval misses memories of concrete knowledge-sharing activities (seminars, teaching, mentoring) when the question is phrased abstractly as 'share knowledge'. The agent searches only variations of the abstract phrase and does not target specific activity verbs, so distinct supporting memories are left out of the answer.
